plan.title: Liver drug-treated vs control QuantSeq 3' DE + GSEA
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a single raw integer gene-level count matrix (/eval-full-32-with-three-prime-n3-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv, 12,000 genes x 6 samples, gene symbols in the first column) with a 6-row sample table (/eval-full-32-with-three-prime-n3-1/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv, one condition column), human liver, 3 drug-treated vs 3 control, unpaired, one batch. The question — which genes differ between treated and control — is a plain two-group count-based differential expression problem, so the plan is one DE track plus one enrichment track plus a consolidated report.

Two dataset facts drive the method choices. First, the library is Lexogen QuantSeq FWD 3' tag-seq: one read per transcript molecule at the 3' end, so a gene's count carries no transcript-length dependence. The counts therefore go into the negative binomial model exactly as STAR/featureCounts produced them — no tximport, no length offset, no TPM/FPKM anywhere in the plan — and the low-count pre-filter uses a lower floor (5 counts in at least 3 samples, the smallest group size) because a floor built for full-length libraries discards a disproportionate share of expressed long genes under 3' tagging. Second, n=3 per group is genuinely underpowered: benchmarks put recovery of true DE genes at a minority of them at this replicate number, concentrated at large fold changes. The plan therefore keeps alpha at 0.05 with BH and independent filtering rather than loosening it to manufacture hits, runs edgeR quasi-likelihood alongside DESeq2 and treats the intersection as the high-confidence set, and requires the report to state the power limit before any gene table — absence from the significant list is not evidence of no change.

QC (blind VST, PCA on the top 500 variable genes, sample-distance heatmap, library sizes) runs first because with 6 samples a single outlier or a swapped label would dominate the fit, and it is cheap to see before testing. Enrichment is preranked fgsea on the full tested list ranked by the DESeq2 Wald statistic — chosen over the shrunken LFC and the signed p-value because it scales the effect by its uncertainty, which matters most at n=3 — against MSigDB human hallmark, with GO BP as the mechanism-level follow-up. Over-representation on the significant list is deliberately not planned: at this power the list will very likely be under ~50 genes, where a hypergeometric test is threshold-driven noise. Both gene set files are human and present in the reference store; the matrix is human liver, so no ortholog mapping is involved.

steps.context: Consumes T1S2 (DESeq2 results, diagnostics), T1S3 (method overlap) and T2S1 (enrichment). No new statistics are computed here beyond assembly and summary.
acceptance_criteria: The power statement appears before any gene table: 3 replicates per group, the share of true effects recoverable at that size per the benchmark literature, and the fold-change range the test can detect
Method, package versions, design formula ~ condition, contrast (condition, treated, control), alpha 0.05 with BH, genes tested after filtering, and genes significant, all stated
MA plot, dispersion plot and p-value histogram included before the gene tables, each with a one-line reading
Gene table gives log2FoldChange, apeglm-shrunken log2FoldChange and lfcSE per gene, ranked by the shrunken value, with the shrinkage estimator named in the header
DESeq2 vs edgeR counts and intersection reported; intersection labelled the high-confidence set
Leading-edge genes listed per significant gene set, with overlaps between reported sets marked
Enrichment section states collection, version, ranking metric (Wald statistic), universe (tested genes) and size window, and notes method-dependence
Reproducibility record stored with the results: sessionInfo, package versions, random seed, gene set collection version
The library type (Lexogen QuantSeq FWD 3' tag-seq) is stated, with the note that TPM/FPKM-style length-normalized units do not apply
constraints: State the power limit at 3 replicates per group before the gene tables; do not adjust the significance threshold to compensate for the small design
Rank genes and draw plots on the shrunken log2 fold change; keep the unshrunken estimate and its standard error in the table
Report the number of significant genes plainly, including if it is zero or very small — do not reach for a looser threshold
Present enrichment hits as hypotheses, naming the method, not as established mechanism
Store the reproducibility record with the results, not as a separate note
caveats: A gene absent from the significant list is not shown to be unchanged — say so explicitly
With 12,000 genes and 6 samples, any single striking gene should be checked against its per-sample counts before it is highlighted

grounding.reason: Report content is set by R-0094 (power statement at 3 replicates first), R-0085/R-0087 (effect columns and fit diagnostics), R-0041/R-0051 (method, versions, thresholds, enrichment provenance), R-0105 (leading edge) and R-0086 (reproducibility record).
